results.title: AngloGold Ashanti, Endeavour Mining host maiden West Africa mine rescue competition
results.content: AngloGold Ashanti's Obuasi Mine and Endeavour Mining have jointly hosted the maiden edition of the West Africa Mine Rescue and Emergency Response Competition (WAMRERC 2026), bringing together emergency response teams from four countries to test their preparedness for mining-related incidents. The five-day competition, held at the Obuasi Mine, involves teams from Ghana, Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire and Senegal. It is aimed at assessing their technical capabilities, encouraging the exchange of knowledge and strengthening cooperation in emergency response across the West African mining industry. Held under the theme, “Together, Saving Lives Through Preparedness and Excellence,” the event is expected to provide a platform for mine rescue professionals to share expertise and build a regional network that can support coordinated responses to emergencies. results.title: Ghana’s UN Mission visits family of Ghanaian killed in second Bronx tragedy, pledges support
results.content: Ghana's Permanent Mission to the United Nations in New York has visited the family of 24-year-old Ghanaian caregiver Joseph Owusu, who was reportedly killed in the Bronx. Joseph Owusu's death comes days after the fatal shooting of 15-year-old Ghanaian Javits Frimpong in the Bronx on October 29, 2026. The two deaths have raised concern among Ghanaians in New York and relatives in Ghana, with calls for investigations and accountability. The visit, led by Deputy Permanent Representative Ben Dotsel Malor and Consul-General Anthony El-Adas, was undertaken on behalf of Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, who joined by phone to express his condolences.

results.title: Beyond the bungalow gates: Why comprehensive sex education and sex negotiation skills are our children’s real protective armor
results.content: The horrifying revelations emerging from Obuasi Senior High Technical School, where up to 19 female students have reportedly come forward detailing alleged sexual exploitation and abuse by members of the school's leadership. Such a report should send chills down the spine of every parent, educator, and policymaker in Ghana. For far too long, our cultural reflex has been one of uncomfortable silence. We treat conversations about adolescent sexuality as a taboo subject. We whisper about puberty behind closed doors while continuing to believe that our teenagers live in a vacuum of innocence. The tragedy at Obuasi SHTS demonstrates that our silence is not protecting our children; it is leaving them defenseless in the face of predatory power dynamics.
